segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Parents were bringing their little kids to Jesus, just so he could put his hands on them and bless them.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: And they brought young children to him, that he should touch them: and his disciples rebuked those that brought them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The disciples tried to wave them off — the Teacher is busy, this is grown-up work, not the place for children.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he saw them do it. And Mark does not soften how he took it.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: But when Jesus saw it, he was much displeased, and said unto them,

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That old word suffer just means let. Let them come. Don't stand in their way. Then he went further.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He meant: nobody earns their way into the kingdom of God. You receive it the way a child receives a gift — with open hands.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he gathered them up in his arms and blessed them, one at a time, unhurried — like there was nowhere else he needed to be.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He had time for the smallest and least important person in the room. That includes you.
